stem:
Sia looks at the diagram of an irregular closed shape drawn on $1\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ squared paper.

Which claim correctly estimates the area of the shape?

options.text: Read the printed label "squared paper" beside the grid as the area value.
Count square units covered by the shape, including reasonable fractions of partly covered squares.
The squared paper is what draws the closed shape, so the grid lines alone are the area.
Add only the length and breadth of a surrounding rectangle and report that sum as the area.

teacher.key_rationale: Area on unit squares is estimated by counting covered square units, with fractions for partial squares. The paper label is not an area. Grid lines do not produce the shape. Rectangle perimeter-style sums are a different mechanism.
teacher.figure_note: Added irregular closed polygon on a unit square grid labelled 1 cm² squares.
